stories.headline: Trump claims a Russia-Ukraine energy truce; Zelensky says it holds only if Moscow reciprocates

key_facts.fact: Trump wrote on Truth Social on Sept. 14 that 'Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy Targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!' — with neither Kyiv nor Moscow confirming any such deal.
key_facts.excerpt: "Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian Energy Targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!" Trump said in a Truth Social post. Neither Ukraine nor Russia has confirmed that such a deal had been struck.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky replied hours later that Ukraine would halt strikes only if partners guarantee Russia stops hitting Ukrainian electricity, energy, critical infrastructure and food movement, adding he is 'not sure' Russia wants any agreement.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine is ready to halt strikes on Russia if its partners ensure that Moscow will refrain from hitting Ukrainian energy facilities, infrastructure and food supply routes, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday. 'Ukraine is not certain that Russia is willing to stick to any agreement,' he wrote.

key_facts.fact: A senior Ukrainian energy official told the Kyiv Independent, on condition of anonymity, that they had heard of no energy ceasefire.
key_facts.excerpt: A top Ukrainian energy official, speaking to the Kyiv Independent on condition of anonymity, said they had not heard of any such energy ceasefire.

key_facts.fact: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Sept. 14 that Russian forces were operating 'across the entire territory of Ukraine and continue to do so — and will continue to do so', while welcoming any call for Kyiv to stop hitting Russian civilian economic infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, asked Monday about the strike on the train near the Polish border, said Russian forces were operating "across the entire territory of Ukraine and continue to do so — and will continue to do so."

key_facts.fact: Trump's push followed US diesel prices hitting a record above an average $6 per gallon on Friday, Sept. 11; he told Zelensky on Sept. 13 to 'stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia'.
key_facts.excerpt: He spoke after diesel prices in the U.S. hit a record on Friday, soaring past an average of $6 per gallon.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky warned against a temporary arrangement that would simply relieve pressure on Moscow ahead of Russia's Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections; the US House Rules Committee on Sept. 14 cleared the Senate-amended Graham sanctions bill for floor action by a 7-3 vote.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ukrainian leader has also warned against a temporary arrangement that would simply give Moscow relief from pressure before Russia's Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections. ... The House Rules Committee on Monday cleared the way for consideration of the Senate-amended Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, reporting the rule by a 7-3 vote.

stories.headline: Houthi missiles wound 13 in three Saudi cities as Riyadh vows a 'firm' response

key_facts.fact: The Saudi-led coalition said on Sept. 15 that Houthi ballistic missiles and drones wounded 13 civilians in Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif on Sept. 14, damaging seven houses and two vehicles.
key_facts.excerpt: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Tuesday that 13 civilians were injured in attacks by the Iran-aligned Houthis on the Saudi cities of Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif on Monday. ... coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Malki said the injuries ranged from minor to moderate and that seven houses and two vehicles were damaged.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia warned on Sept. 15 it would react 'firmly' to the Houthis, who had seized Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait the previous week.
key_facts.excerpt: Saudi Arabia warned Tuesday it will react "firmly" to Yemen's Houthis, after a series of attacks carried out by the pro-Iranian rebels using ballistic missiles and drones wounded 13 civilians in the country's south. ... The group seized control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait last week.

key_facts.fact: The Houthis said they fired dozens of missiles and drones at the Khamis Mushait airbase on Sept. 14, targeting hangars, radars, runways and ammunition depots in retaliation for Saudi airstrikes in Yemen.
key_facts.excerpt: The Houthis on Monday said they fired dozens of missiles and drones at a military airbase in Khamis Mushait in southern Saudi Arabia, targeting aircraft hangars, radar systems, runways and ammunition depots in retaliation for Saudi airstrikes in Yemen.

key_facts.fact: Traders estimate a prolonged shutdown of Saudi Arabia's 7 million barrel-per-day East-West pipeline, knocked offline by an attack Riyadh blames on Iran-backed militias in Iraq, could remove as much as 4% of global oil supply while Hormuz stays largely blockaded.
key_facts.excerpt: Traders said a prolonged shutdown of the Saudi pipeline could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply while the strait is largely blockaded. Riyadh has not said when operations might resume.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command publicly rejected the IRGC's Sept. 14 claim that the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia struck a naval mine, saying the ship was disabled by an Iranian missile last month and hit again by an Iranian drone over the weekend off Oman.
key_facts.excerpt: CENTCOM said, "The Panama-flagged oil tanker El Gaia was struck by an Iranian missile last month and rendered inoperable. This weekend, Iran struck the tanker again with a drone while the ship sat in waters off the coast of Oman."

key_facts.fact: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Sept. 14 that Tehran is ready for talks including on its nuclear programme if Washington lifts sanctions and stops negotiating through military pressure, while Trump said the US is 'open' to the 'concept' of a deal.
key_facts.excerpt: "We are ready for dialogue," Pezeshkian told India Today ... "the United States should lift its sanctions, abandon unilateralism, not speak to us through force." ... "The failing Nation of Iran wants to make a deal, quickly and badly," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

stories.headline: 10-year Treasury yield breaks 5% for the first time since 2023 as $107 oil forces a Fed hike

key_facts.fact: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield briefly breached 5% during Monday's New York session, the first time since 2023, closing at 4.99% and rebounding above 5.04% on Tuesday.
key_facts.excerpt: That tracked a drop in Treasuries in New York session, when the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield briefly breached the 5% mark for the first time since 2023. The yield on the 10-year was at 4.99% in Asian trading Tuesday.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude climbed 1.3% to almost $107 a barrel, extending September gains to more than 18%, with Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline still offline.
key_facts.excerpt: Global benchmark Brent climbed 1.3% to almost $107 a barrel, extending the gains this month to over 18%. Oil pushed higher as traders weighed risks to Middle East supplies, with a critical Saudi Arabian pipeline still offline after attacks.

key_facts.fact: CME FedWatch pricing put the odds of a Fed rate increase on Wednesday at roughly 93%, which would be the first hike in more than three years and the first of Kevin Warsh's chairmanship.
key_facts.excerpt: Markets now see a Fed hike on Wednesday as a near certainty, with CME's FedWatch tool pricing in a roughly 93% chance of an interest-rate increase, which would be the first in more than three years.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs flipped its call from no change to a 25bp hike after August CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month and 3.4% year-on-year, with core CPI up 0.3%, and producer prices up 0.4% on the month and 5.4% on the year.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs has changed its call for this week's Federal Reserve meeting, now expecting a 25-basis-point rate increase after previously forecasting no change. ... August CPI rose 0.4% from July and 3.4% from a year earlier, while core inflation increased 0.3% on the month, stronger than expected. Producer prices had already risen 0.4% in August and 5.4% from a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: Gold fell for a second straight session to around $4,285 an ounce, after touching a one-month low of $4,253, as higher yields and a firmer dollar cut demand for the non-yielding metal.
key_facts.excerpt: Gold fell for a second consecutive day to trade around $4,285 an ounce as higher rates typically diminish the appeal of the non-yielding metal.

key_facts.fact: The Fed's current rate is about 3.6%, and a hike would lift the target range to 3.75%-4.00% — against Trump's public demand for a cut.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to lift its short-term interest rate Wednesday for the first time in three years to fight stubbornly high inflation, a move that would put the central bank at odds with President Donald Trump's support for a cut. An increase in the Fed's rate, currently about 3.6%, isn't guaranteed.

stories.headline: Michael Dell's family office and Sequence take insurance broker Baldwin private for $7.7 billion

key_facts.fact: Baldwin Group (Nasdaq: BWIN) said on Sept. 14 it agreed to an all-cash take-private valued at about $7.7 billion by an entity formed by Sequence Holdings and DFO Management, Michael Dell's family investment office.
key_facts.excerpt: The Baldwin Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: BWIN) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement under which an entity to be formed by Sequence Holdings and DFO Management will acquire a majority interest in the Company in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $7.7 billion.

key_facts.fact: Shareholders get $32.50 a share in cash, an approximately 88% premium to Baldwin's unaffected June 17 closing price before reports of a possible deal.
key_facts.excerpt: Baldwin shareholders will receive $32.50 apiece in cash, implying a premium of about 88% to the stock's June 17 closing — the unaffected share price before media reports emerged about a potential deal.

key_facts.fact: The $7.7 billion enterprise value breaks down into roughly $4.6 billion of equity and about $3.1 billion of net debt assumed or refinanced; there is no financing condition.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction implies a total enterprise value of approximately $7.7 billion, comprised of an equity purchase price of approximately $4.6 billion and approximately $3.1 billion of net debt assumed or refinanced ... The consummation of the transaction is not subject to any financing condition.

key_facts.fact: Reuters framed the rationale as giving the insurance broker greater flexibility to pursue AI investments; Sequence is described as an AI-focused holding company.
key_facts.excerpt: will take Baldwin Group private in a $7.7 billion deal, the companies said on Monday, providing the insurance broker greater flexibility to pursue AI investments.

key_facts.fact: Eligible Baldwin employees keep a significant minority equity stake, and the deal is expected to close in Q1 2027 subject to shareholder and regulatory approval.
key_facts.excerpt: Baldwin will become a privately held company, with eligible Baldwin colleagues retaining a significant minority equity stake ... The transaction is expected to close in Q1 2027, subject to approval by Baldwin shareholders.

stories.headline: Vega-C launches FLEX and Sentinel-3C, first satellite to map plant fluorescence from orbit

key_facts.fact: Flight VV30 lifted off from Europe's Spaceport in French Guiana on 15 September at 03:21 CEST (22:21 local time on 14 September), carrying ESA's FLEX Earth Explorer and the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite.
key_facts.excerpt: Flight VV30 lifted off on 15 September at 03:21 (14 September at 22:21 local time). ... The European Space Agency's FLEX Earth Explorer satellite and the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite have been launched together aboard a Vega-C rocket.

key_facts.fact: A Vespa launch adapter let both satellites stack inside the Vega-C fairing; Sentinel-3C was injected into orbit first, with FLEX separating roughly an hour later, and ESA's control centre in Germany received first signal from both.
key_facts.excerpt: Positioned on top of Vespa, Sentinel-3C was injected into orbit first, followed by FLEX approximately one hour later. ... ESA's European Space Operations Centre in Germany received the all-important first signal from each satellite.

key_facts.fact: FLEX weighs about 400 kg, flies at 814 km in tandem with a Sentinel-3 satellite, and has a 3.5-year planned mission; Thales Alenia Space's ESA contract for it was worth about €150 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The FLEX satellite weighs about 400 kilograms. It will operate in a Sun-synchronous orbit at an altitude of 814 kilometers, with a full observation cycle repeating every 27 days. The planned mission duration is three and a half years ... its contract with ESA was worth approximately €150 million.

key_facts.fact: FLEX is the first satellite designed specifically to detect plant fluorescence from orbit, using the Leonardo-built FLORIS spectrometer at 300 m resolution as a proxy for vegetation health and stress.
key_facts.excerpt: FLEX follows, riding a Vespa+R adapter to an 814 km orbit where its FLORIS spectrometer will map the faint fluorescence plants emit during photosynthesis, a proxy for vegetation health and stress at 300 m resolution. ... FLEX is the first satellite designed specifically to detect plant fluorescence from orbit.

key_facts.fact: Sentinel-3C, weighing about 1,143 kg, joins Sentinels 3A and 3B in a sun-synchronous orbit around 820 km, continuing Copernicus ocean, land, ice and atmosphere monitoring; VV30 was only the second Vega-C flight managed solely by Avio.
key_facts.excerpt: The VV30 mission will be the second managed solely by Italian company, Avio, and not jointly with Arianespace. This will also be the second Vega-C launch of 2026 and the eighth overall.

stories.headline: BioNTech's gotistobart nearly doubles survival vs chemo in previously treated squamous lung cancer

key_facts.fact: BioNTech and OncoC4 reported on Sept. 14 the first median overall survival data from stage 1 of the Phase 3 PRESERVE-003 trial of gotistobart (BNT316/ONC-392) in squamous non-small cell lung cancer that progressed on prior immunotherapy and chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: BioNTech SE (Nasdaq: BNTX) and OncoC4, Inc. today announced the first median overall survival ("OS") data from the non-pivotal stage 1 of the global randomized PRESERVE-003 Phase 3 clinical trial (NCT05671510) of gotistobart.

key_facts.fact: Median overall survival was 18.5 months with gotistobart versus 10.0 months with docetaxel (HR 0.56; nominal p=0.0295), at a July 17, 2026 data cut-off with 25.4 months median follow-up across 87 randomized patients.
key_facts.excerpt: The median OS was 18.5 months for patients treated with gotistobart compared to 10.0 months for patients treated with docetaxel (HR: 0.56; nominal p-value=0.0295).

key_facts.fact: Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 44.4% of gotistobart patients (20/45) versus 48.8% on docetaxel (20/42).
key_facts.excerpt: Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events ("AEs") were reported in 20/45 (44.4%) patients receiving gotistobart and 20/42 (48.8%) patients receiving docetaxel.

key_facts.fact: Gotistobart is a CTLA-4-targeting immunotherapy designed to deplete regulatory T cells inside the tumour microenvironment; the pivotal stage 2 of PRESERVE-003 is running at more than 160 sites globally.
key_facts.excerpt: Gotistobart is an investigational CTLA-4-targeting immunotherapy designed to selectively deplete regulatory T cells ("Tregs") within the tumor microenvironment ... The pivotal stage 2 portion of PRESERVE-003 is currently ongoing at more than 160 sites globally.

key_facts.fact: The data were presented at the IASLC 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer; gotistobart holds FDA Fast Track (2022) and Orphan Drug (2025) designations and China NMPA Breakthrough Therapy designation (2025).
key_facts.excerpt: The data were presented at the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer ("IASLC") 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer ("WCLC"). ... Gotistobart received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. FDA in 2022 ... and Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of patients with squamous NSCLC in 2025.

sources.title: BioNTech and OncoC4 Present Updated Data Showing Gotistobart Nearly Doubled Median Overall Survival versus Standard-of-Care Chemotherapy in Previously Treated Squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Patients
